candidates.description: Miao Yin the Panda By Christie Kotz ThePeachPeddler 15 inches (38.1 centimeters) Allow me to introduce my latest teddybear, "Miao Yin" (named after the character in Big Trouble in Little China) Here are a few details about this little lady: ~ She is made with Steiff Schulte Mohair (black parts including eye patches) and Alpaca (cream sections), fully lined with cotton backing ~ Blue handpainted glass eyes (by Edinburgh Imports) ~ 100% handsewn ~ Embroidered nose sealed with beeswax ~ Handshaded with artist oil paints to fill out the eye patches (which are inset black mohair pieces) and shade around the face ~ Ultrasuede pads with sculpted toes ~ Weighted with copper coated steel shot (in pouches to prevent the shot from wandering through the stuffing) - actual weight = 3.5 pounds ~ She is a sitting bear, and is not made to stand. I don't make many pandas, and very very rarely do the inset eye patches (versus painting/shading in the eye spots), so this girl is pretty special. :)

categories: Collections of the Hunterian Museum, London
candidates.description: Skull of a female giant panda (Ailuropoda melanoleuca) named Ming donated by London Zoo. The specimen is from the Hunterian Museum at the Royal College of Surgeons of England. Ming was one of the first giant pandas ever seen in the United Kingdom. In 1938, an animal collector brought six pandas from China to London. Three of these animals were purchased by the Zoological Society of London for London Zoo. The playful cub Ming became a national celebrity at the Zoo and a favourite of photographers like Bert Hardy . The air raids on London meant she was evacuated from the Zoo several times. Ming became a symbol of hope during the Second World War. Pandas are delicate creatures. At this time, little was known about caring for them. By 1940 Ming was the only living panda in Europe. She died after an unidentified illness in 1944. The Royal College of Surgeons carried out a full post-mortem examination. The top of the skull has been removed to try to determine the cause of death.
